tagline: DistributionNOW is a premier global provider of pipes, valves, fittings, pumps and fabricated equipment for energy and industrial infrastructure.
hero_kpi_rationale: Total Revenue is the fundamental KPI for DNOW, reflecting demand in its key end markets (upstream, midstream, gas utilities, downstream and industrial). It is directly linked to customer capital expenditures in traditional energy and energy transition, including data centers and hydrogen.

risks.title: Oil and Natural Gas Price Volatility
risks.score_rationale: Volatility in oil and natural gas prices directly affects upstream customer capital expenditures and sales volumes. Oil prices declined 14.5% in 2025, negatively impacting demand. (Item 1A Risk Factors, MD&A p. 36)

risks.title: Steel Price and Supply Chain Disruptions
risks.score_rationale: The majority of distributed products contain steel. Price fluctuations and supply disruptions directly affect availability and profitability. (Item 1A Risk Factors, MD&A p. 36)

risks.title: Manufacturer and Distributor Inventory Levels
risks.score_rationale: Elevated inventory levels among manufacturers and other distributors can create overcapacity and reduce prices, impacting profitability. (Item 1A Risk Factors, MD&A p. 36)

risks.title: Tariffs and Trade Policy Uncertainty
risks.score_rationale: Tariffs on steel and imported products can increase product costs and affect the company's competitiveness. (Item 1A Risk Factors)

risks.title: Customer Capital Expenditure Dependence
risks.score_rationale: DNOW is heavily dependent on customer capital expenditures for exploration, production, processing and maintenance of energy infrastructure. (MD&A Key Drivers, p. 36)

risks.title: Energy Transition and Market Structural Changes
risks.score_rationale: The transition to alternative energy sources (carbon capture, hydrogen, offshore wind) requires adaptation of product and service offerings. (Item 1A Risk Factors, MD&A p. 36)

ai_positioning.summary: DNOW is not an AI developer but benefits indirectly from growth in AI infrastructure and energy transition. The company supplies essential components (pipes, valves, fabricated equipment) for data centers, LNG facilities and hydrogen projects that support the energy ecosystem for AI.
evidence: DNOW supplies PVF, pumps and fabricated equipment for data centers, LNG facilities and RNG facilities
The company supports carbon capture and utilization projects, biofuels and hydrogen processing facilities
Critical infrastructure for energy transition aligned with computational demand needs
